question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Intervals on Which a Function is Invertible Given Its Graph
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/1597ad53471d0d9b44812c5caa31bcb160cfa150d1df9a9314447fa49e62ccff.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible?

I. $x\in [-6,0]$

II. $x\in [-6,4)$

III. $x\in [4,10)$
question.worked_solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.  

- The given function is invertible on each of the intervals $x\in [-6,0]$ and $x\in [4,10).$ Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/7cb282e3fa66af801ff03816973d5f5f1d0cb41e39d08a8addd27d7aa9c5b9df.png)

      

- The given function is **not** invertible on the interval $[-6,4]$  because some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/000953609a7b3e13ad09473ead62f96aa895c7f94aa618884e69883595004fd4.png)

 

 Therefore, the correct answer is "I  and III only".
